# Nathan Magsig Declares Victory in Senate District 12
---
|
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** November 10th, 2026Contact: nathan@nathanmagsig.com
---
| | | | | |
**Nathan Magsig Declares Victory in Senate District 12**
**FRESNO, CA** – Today, Nathan Magsig declared victory in California’s 12th State Senate District. The Associated Press has also called the race for Magsig.
“I am honored by the trust the voters of Senate District 12 have placed in me,” said Magsig. “Throughout this campaign, I heard from families struggling with rising costs, farmers who need reliable water supplies, and communities concerned about crime, wildfire, and the availability of insurance. I am ready to take those concerns to Sacramento and fight for the people who call this district home.”
Magsig campaigned on lowering costs, strengthening public safety, securing reliable water supplies, and improving forest management. He will bring his experience as a Fresno County Supervisor, former Clovis Mayor, and small business owner to the State Senate.
“I want to thank my Lord and savior Jesus Christ, my family, our volunteers, and every supporter who knocked on doors, made calls, put up a sign, or shared our message,” Magsig continued. “This victory reflects the hard work of so many people who believe our communities deserve a stronger voice in Sacramento.”
“To everyone in Senate District 12, whether you voted for me or not, I will work hard to earn your trust. I look forward to serving you and delivering results for our Valley and mountain communities.”
---
| | ###
Senator-Elect Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor and former Mayor of Clovis. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)

Peter,
Last week, in sweeping and decisive victories, the American people rebuked the depravity, corruption, and incompetence of the failed lame duck President Donald J. Trump.
But, Peter, amidst our celebration, we must acknowledge that the underlying crisis gripping our Republic remains — and that therefore our most vital work lies ahead.
[**Right now, while the wind is at our back, I’m asking for $5 or whatever you can give to help carry our historic movement forward. We still need you, Peter.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&amount=5&t=2&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)
**[CONTRIBUTE $5](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&amount=5&t=3&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)**
Our work isn’t finished yet, Peter.
While the wealthy and well-lobbied feast on inside information and official favors, America's forgotten families face systemic corporate disrespect and official indifference, working harder and harder while the treadmill just gets faster and steeper, and the bills get higher and higher.
Instead of reading your daughter her favorite book that precious spare hour after work, you're on the phone begging the insurance company to cover the medicine that prevents her seizures.
You report the black mold to your landlord, who doesn't fix the leak, and the ambulance for your toddler's asthma attack is followed by a $3,000 bill.
For too many, home ownership’s a fantasy. Family farms face ruin. And while health care’s never cost more, plastics invade our bodies, blood, and breast milk. Toxic forever chemicals taint half the country's drinking water, and polluters have been granted fresh license to poison our air.
You’ve seen that abroad, American credibility and leadership are in decay while the world re-arms for global conflict.
You see that at our grave peril, humanity is fast forgetting the terrible lessons of two World Wars and the Holocaust.
Meanwhile, you see the titans of Silicon Valley digging bunkers for themselves and warning that the artificial intelligence they're creating risks human extinction.
And amidst these challenges of unprecedented consequence and complexity, though we rightly celebrate this historic victory, the fact is we’ve been too long mired in a small and selfish politics — a politics bought by big money, unmoored from fixed moral principles, and resigned to intractable division.
In other words, the United States has been adrift in a gale.
But we can and will reclaim control over our own destiny — not just through this historic landslide victory, but through all the vital work that follows it.
You know that my team’s work doesn’t end just because we’ve won the election. We still have bills to pay and we still need your help to keep building this movement.
[**I know it’s a lot to ask after a grueling cycle, but if you’re able, please donate whatever you can today. Our work is far from over.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&t=4&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)
**[CONTRIBUTE $5](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&amount=5&t=5&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)**
Thanks for continuing to be part of this team,
Jon

name: Coach Tommy Tuberville
subject: Thank you!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TUBERVILLE FOR GOVERNOR, INC
body:
We Won!
| Peter,

**We Won!**
[](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=2e058647f35142d0b8b0247df4436bc4&_e=4fQknZsi46KXyD1GAVvhdmu1Vw2_KarEkj1npq9TUXQcuELw4jJldEXlHX6VEV9k8VVXN4Tu67d9OmAbKO7ZKpqCkFEQIMzer8Xv3JGKH5mbN5f9oCPywEimv7Tl3t13YlExqWVysgZEScqohznPXN4Le4rP7qa0cC_AaJIG3FyxDerFmX8nMONm5qgJ_ipBTNuMP7BzHycpixBAuhb-RK9YgmEI9YzXUyqGVeILq-OCAtNvKfjQTU6WHjacVXXpOYe8bwNmgVT80lgYuc-1gj_8NZR3YMxpYGhIlXKvfmyZkv3IYxiTGVUWvCUnGErauLMPd3YhzIRKGmWS-ewmqsNecun08eaQrhtxkU_0esV9iEsuEvCSvKKhl66l1EJZYe95WEBR8w5YteHWufBLjrItY88Xs-dbeKd1pbNWe_1z634M_dV9Rnl_EAgMrBgACmPg8q95F6pswQFstR418_ZOA8dt2NsniJi7NtetELU8XaSSukr-eDti-fk0WjBPpvLPqob6fW9wEuvsIvRrs0s9MmgoHRHvOL65JKMA3TI%3D)
_I want to start by saying thank you, from the bottom of my heart._ _**I love this state, and I’m honored to serve as Alabama’s 55th Governor.**_

_This campaign was never about me. It was about Alabama. It was about people who believe this state should put its citizens first, protect its values, and make its own decisions, not let Washington make them for us.

You showed up. You worked. You voted. And because of you, we’re moving forward together.

I’ve been a coach most of my life, and I’ve been in a lot of locker rooms after big wins. The best ones aren’t where people celebrate the loudest. They’re where everybody understands the work that got them there.

That’s how I feel today.

There’s a lot of work ahead, and I don’t take it lightly. I’ll be governor for every Alabamian, whether they voted for me or not. And we’re starting from a position of strength because of the people who stood with this campaign from day one._

_**Thank you for your trust.
Thank you for your support.
Thank you for believing that Alabama’s best days are still ahead.**_

_I’m ready to get to work.

God bless,
Coach Tommy Tuberville _

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: President AOC? It's not a joke anymore.
body:
Plus: New Mexico Democrats hit the supermajority | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/10NN6ZPuuZu?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Last Tuesday was brutal. No way around it.
[So this week I brought in Republican pollster Jeff Glassburner to tell us what actually happened.](https://us.list-manage.com/kb8aCAlifju?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) Independents didn’t just lean left, they voted like Democrats. New Mexico now has a 47-23 supermajority in the House. And the Senate isn’t coming back for a while.
Then I asked Jeff which Democrat worries him most in 2028. He said AOC
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/7JqRRPGmBKm?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
**🔥 INDEPENDENTS DIDN’T LEAN DEMOCRAT. THEY VOTED LIKE DEMOCRATS.**
Pollsters nailed where Republicans would land. Then the undecideds broke 30, 40, 50 points the other way, depending on the state. Jeff says independents haven’t voted as one bloc like this since Watergate.
This was not a turnout collapse. Jeff explains what it was instead, and why that’s harder to fix.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/32gbEne4MGt?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**🚨 JD VANCE SAYS IT WAS IRAN. JEFF SAYS LOOK AT LAST YEAR.**
The vice president blamed the war this week. Jeff points to two governor’s races a full year ago that showed the same number everyone’s shocked by now.
Republicans lost Mississippi, Kansas and Texas on the same night. Jeff has one line about what that means for the party that I couldn’t argue with either.

**🏛️ DEMOCRATS NOW HAVE A SUPERMAJORITY IN SANTA FE.**
Rebecca Dow is out. Luis Terrazas is out. Democrats hold exactly two-thirds of the New Mexico House.
I pulled Eddy, Lea and Chaves County turnout and compared it to 2022. The population went up. Republican turnout went the other way.
There’s also a registration number that changes how we look at 2030.

**⚠️ PRESIDENT AOC. IT’S NO JOKE.**
Jeff says Republicans are underestimating AOC “to an extreme degree.” She’s going to own the rooms in Iowa, South Carolina and Nevada, and the center of the Democratic Party has nobody left who can box her out the way Biden boxed out Bernie.
Then we walk through the 2028 Senate map. Six seats, none of them deep red, and a road back that probably runs through 2030.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/Qn5vvWFREA3?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**PLUS:** Why Trump “likes it when his proteges fight,” 65 House seats in play for 2028, Jeff’s three-word advice for the White House, and the prediction bet Krysty lost. Ella may not get dinner this week.
---
|
---

Pennsylvania is home to over 600,000

courage, honor, and integrity.

remember our nation’s veterans, I want to extend my sincere gratitude to

Thank you for your commitment to service and our Constitution.

Thank you for having our backs. I promise, I’ll always have yours.

Wishing you a happy Veterans Day,

Josh Shapiro

subject: Happy Veterans Day, Michigan
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Happy Veterans Day, Michigan.

As the wife of a combat veteran, I’ve seen firsthand the sacrifices our
military service members, their families, and veterans make every single
day.

To Michigan’s hundreds of thousands of veterans: Thank you for your
service. We honor you, and we’re committed to supporting you and your
families every day.

I know we have a long way to go to ensure every Michigan veteran has
access to healthcare, to mental health support, and to housing, but I can
tell you this: we’ll always go above and beyond to serve and support our
veterans. They’re our community too.

As your Governor, I’ll use every tool in my toolbox to make sure we’re
serving and protecting those who served and protected us.

Happy Veterans Day, Michigan.

Gratefully,
Jocelyn Benson

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with supporters like you.

name: Tim Walz
subject: Proud to have served
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Today, I’m thinking about my fellow veterans and the families who stand beside them.
#
Peter,
Two days after my 17th birthday, my dad drove me to meet a lieutenant who had a farm near our house. He got off his tractor to administer my oath of enlistment right there in his cornfield.
Raising my right hand to join the National Guard was one of the best decisions I ever made. I was proud to wear our country’s uniform for the next 24 years.
During those years, I learned a lot about hard work, service, and looking out for the people beside you. Those lessons have stayed with me ever since.
Today, on Veterans Day, I’m thinking about everyone who has answered that call to serve, along with the families who have stood beside them through long absences, uncertainty, and sacrifice.
**We owe them more than a thank-you. We owe them the care and support they’ve earned, long after they take off the uniform.** That means access to health care, a safe place to call home, and a community that has their back.
If there’s a veteran in your life, reach out today. Ask how they’re doing. Let them know you’re thinking of them. And let’s keep looking out for them the other 364 days of the year, too.
To my fellow veterans and your families: Thank you. It’s an honor to stand with you.
Tim

## Johnson Picked to Be Next Lt. Governor
Senate Republicans [nominated Franklin Sen. Before we get into it, please consider becoming a paid subscriber to help us produce articles like this throughout the year and hold Congress accountable._

I started The Angry Democrat because I believe we have the most say when our own party is in power. That's when we should get off the sidelines, speak directly to the people we elected, and hold them to the promises they made to us.

I want healthcare for all, a balanced budget and a lower national debt, a ban on stock trading in Congress and the executive branch, and term limits across all three branches of government. I also want to end corruption, reform campaign finance, and overturn _Citizens United_.
That starts with a record we can come back to: who gave to the campaigns, who spent money independently, and how far we can trace that money.

* * *
## What the Eight (Dem) Campaigns Reported
Through the **October 14, 2026 reporting cutoff** , the eight campaigns reported approximately:
* **$24.65 million** in total receipts.
* **$21.82 million** in campaign spending.
* **$6.55 million** from other political committees, about **27%** of total receipts.

Political committee contributions include money from corporate-affiliated PACs, labor PACs, trade association PACs, and other political committees.
**OH-1: Greg Landsman**
* Campaign receipts: **$5.66 million**
* Campaign spending: **$5.34 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.20 million**

**OH-3: Joyce Beatty**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.45 million**
* Campaign spending: **$1.43 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.05 million** , about **72%** of receipts

**OH-7: Brian Poindexter**
* Campaign receipts: **$3.72 million**
* Campaign spending: **$2.93 million**
* From other political committees: **$401,000**

**OH-9: Marcy Kaptur**
* Campaign receipts: **$5.91 million**
* Campaign spending: **$5.66 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.51 million** , the highest dollar amount among the eight campaigns

**OH-10: Kristina Knickerbocker**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.02 million**
* Campaign spending: **$882,000**
* From other political committees: **$90,500**

**OH-11: Shontel Brown**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.57 million**
* Campaign spending: **$1.18 million**
* From other political committees: **$984,000** , about **63%** of receipts

**OH-13: Emilia Sykes**
* Campaign receipts: **$3.99 million**
* Campaign spending: **$3.17 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.26 million**

**OH-15: Don Leonard**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.33 million**
* Campaign spending: **$1.23 million**
* From other political committees: **$50,000**

* * *
## Outside Spending, District by District
Independent expenditures are separate from campaign receipts and spending. A group can pay for an ad opposing Max Miller without sending any money to Brian Poindexter's campaign.
The lists below show spending **for the Democrat** , **against the Democrat** , and **against the Republican opponent**. They don't include every category of spending in each race. The general election figures for OH-7, OH-9, OH-10, and OH-15 use filings through November 9. The other district totals and some individual spending categories come from the earlier working compilation. Those figures remain provisional until late notices and amendments are reconciled with regular filings.
### OH-1: Greg Landsman
**Outside spending**
* Supporting Landsman: **$1.80 million**
* Opposing Landsman: **$3.61 million**
* Opposing his Republican opponent: **$868,000**

**Selected spending supporting Landsman**
* **CFFE PAC:** About **$643,000**
* **New American Jobs Fund:** About **$507,000**
* **A Strong Innovation Economy Requires Strong IP Protection:** About **$240,000**

**Vendor status:** Specific payees and advertising formats remain unverified.
### OH-3: Joyce Beatty
**Outside spending identified**
* Supporting Beatty: About **$160**
* Opposing Beatty: **None identified** in the records reviewed
* Opposing her Republican opponent: About **$185**

**Groups identified:** Sierra Club Independent Action and Stand Up for Ohio. Direct committee contributions were the larger source of funding in this race.
### OH-7: Brian Poindexter vs. Max Miller
**General election outside spending**
* Supporting Poindexter: About **$740,000**
* Opposing Poindexter: About **$6.8 million**
* Opposing Miller: About **$11.2 million**
* Combined spending supporting Poindexter or opposing Miller: About **$11.9 million**

**Selected general election expenditures**
* **House Majority PAC:** **$6.83 million** in television advertising opposing Miller
* **Your Community PAC:** **$1.98 million** in television advertising opposing Miller
* **Ready for the Fight:** **$1.47 million** in media buys opposing Miller

## Who Funded the Outside Groups?
The amounts below are **national contributions to the committees**. They show who gave to a group that spent money in Ohio. A separate record would be needed to show that a donor's money paid for a particular Ohio ad.
### House Majority PAC
* **House Majority Forward:** About **$93.7 million**. The nonprofit's underlying donors are not fully identified in the PAC's filings.
* **Michael Bloomberg:** **$16 million**
* **Reid Hoffman:** **$8.5 million**
* **Ohio spending identified:** Television opposing Max Miller, Mike Turner, and Derek Merrin, plus spending opposing Mike Carey.

### Your Community PAC
* **American Opportunity Action:** **$10.015 million** in one filing-based compilation. The amount varies across the records reviewed and remains provisional.
* **Sixteen Thirty Fund:** About **$2.74 million**
* **United Futures:** About **$2.58 million**
* **Green Advocacy Project:** **$2 million**
* **Ohio spending identified:** Television opposing Max Miller and Mike Turner, digital advertising supporting Kristina Knickerbocker, and spending supporting Don Leonard and opposing Mike Carey.

### Ready for the Fight
* **JB Pritzker:** About **$10 million** , as identified in the working research.
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$1.47 million** on media opposing Max Miller.

### Jobs and Democracy PAC
* **Public First Action:** About **$15.4 million** across two reported name variants
* **Public First PAC:** About **$4.05 million**
* **Jan Leike:** **$100,000** in personal contributions
* **Girish Sastry:** **$75,000** in personal contributions
* **Todor Markov:** **$50,000** in personal contributions
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$570,204** supporting Brian Poindexter in the earlier filing snapshot. The records reviewed do not establish that Anthropic corporate funds paid for those ads.

### Think Big PAC
* **Leading the Future:** **$20 million** across four matched transfers in one filing-based compilation. Think Big reported **$24.5 million** in total political committee receipts. The full amount attributable to Leading the Future still needs reconciliation.
* **Upstream contributors to Leading the Future:** The research identified **a16z Capital Management** and personal contributions from **Greg and Anna Brockman**.
* **Ron Conway:** **$500,000** directly to Think Big
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$332,071** supporting Emilia Sykes.

### CFFE PAC
* **Pivotal Ventures:** **$2 million**
* **Opportunity Action Fund:** Identified as a contributor, with materially different totals across the compilations reviewed.
* **Ohio spending identified:** Support for Greg Landsman, Marcy Kaptur, Emilia Sykes, and Don Leonard.

### New Democrat Majority
* **Opportunity Forward Alliance:** About **$3.36 million**
* **Effective Governing Coalition:** **$2.25 million**
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$270,000** for digital advertising and production supporting Emilia Sykes.

## Who Received the Payments?
The committee paying for an ad, the firm it hires, and the station or platform that runs it can be three different entities. Here's what the vendor research identifies so far:
* **Jobs and Democracy PAC -> Bryson Gillette LLC:** About **$19.43 million nationwide**. The national vendor total does not tell us how much the firm received for the Poindexter spending.
* **Think Big PAC -> Lantern Production Consultants LLC:** About **$22.33 million nationwide**. The vendor compilation links Lantern to a roughly **$4,900 media placement fee** supporting Sykes. That fee is part of the **$332,071** in spending supporting her.
* **Think Big PAC -> Manhattan Strategies LLC:** About **$574,000 nationwide**. No Sykes-specific amount is identified here.
* **BDA PAC -> possible Bottled Lightning Collective payment:** The research points to Bottled Lightning as a possible direct-mail vendor for the roughly **$198,000** supporting Poindexter. The original payee record still needs confirmation.

## DMV Launches ‘Open Your Eyes’ Campaign
The Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles has [_launched a statewide campaign_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO6zAMBdDV2B0DSf4XKl7jLq-d0mAs2iEgfyBxZGT3A02QFQw7gsDFPfy6T3dkz_v6HzeykpZppyt6EqEwHSftr-M70IvijNuJvO7Lg49lMsq0oDVoPeEsnGiqsXR2wZpwKMnqbqiroWmaqnzavu6WoTNoGlJKDY3rjFNaqRo7fBBVJducp99jKn2jztHQP3rdtNjrlopakWM5wk2elDisvDMu_nUkCrf52EpvnyJnLKp_hRkLM16RJB8KM2ZPYUZ_zOjfK3wSwG0JMhKyEjITPk4QDCtJBMdRAs5CDlzgxPsKUVDoYkfAO-TqZbDuvNh7jm1X1GrdkP1vMfnjT5M1PwEAAP__4zSOtA) called “Open Your Eyes” that compares glancing at your phone behind the wheel to driving with your eyes shut. The centerpiece television ad shows two distracted drivers covering their faces with their hands, then freezes time an instant before they collide. It began rolling out this month across broadcast, streaming, and digital services. So far in 2026, Virginia State Police data show [_11,953 crashes_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LvO3CAQBeCnwR0rg_GtoEjjbtOmtGZhsEfCF8HYq337iET7BP_Uo6Nzvj_P-QkUaV9-w4aW7zDv-M4RmTHNx4n757gSfjA72E6gZQ8vOsKsa91JpaRSMzimG2cDlbcBDMJYoVX9aJqxbdumWi0MXoNRvnPB904NvglD0zvTvsJYj8ZVZEue-n-6UQ_sPY7Da1BtB4PqUJgaPfGRHrziTWmhnSDEz3Fjerhjq6Jdmc8sml9CT0JPcC1XZggJ8UyYc3kSeirbhJ6-CdJvt4xw7W7FLGFnkp4yJ3CMXvpENyb5HS55BZbEWTqIRUwWHll8ZAESeqqS9eebYqTc9cLUywYU__XjH9LeVv8NAAD__7tFk0o), 93 deaths, and 816 serious injuries involving a distracted driver. About 10% of those drivers were distracted by cellphone use or texting. The campaign was developed to “shift the mindset of those who see no harm in taking their eyes off the road,” said DMV Commissioner Saundra Jack, the Governor’s Highway Safety Representative.
## Lawmakers Weigh Tougher Plate-Reader Rules
A Virginia State Crime Commission report found seven police [_agencies reported keeping license-plate reader data_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OrSAUhZ9GOw0giBYUt7E7t52SbGCjO8GfQY7mvP3kzGSeYFb9rbWS7-NhH0CJtvk_rGjKFe2G95mwFMx2P3B77c-MLzw9rAfQvEVHe7SCib7hvOHcgi90oZVQBxNBIow1Gq5H2Y1Kqa5ejGMxdhC1F9rB6Mage6dQ9jLwKLQaajLvPf4T0fEWdcBxcANXPQy8x0oyDFT23JYFL8ozbQQxvfYLc-v3tU5mKeU4q-5fJaZKTPd9v1GPW8F8fj4h45urxPTbrsQEuZBPaLWEIDmDhjPmGxmdagCFarrBMY8AvB98u5Q11dmE46aU6Ox1Jdm8AqXv__JHdZcRXwEAAP__GzWDhA) longer than the state’s 21-day limit, including one that held mobile-camera data for 90 days. That’s down from 33 in the commission’s January report. Of the 351 agencies that responded to the survey, 191 said they use the cameras. Most reported complying, though six lacked a required policy and a few improperly shared data with federal or out-of-state agencies. Twenty agencies reported unauthorized use by employees, and seven criminal charges had been filed in two Virginia general district courts as of October, all still pending. Hampton Commonwealth’s Attorney Anton Bell, a commission member, said the cameras have clear benefits but need “checks and balances.” Richmond and Henrico have already [_moved to end their camera contracts_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAQx58GO8wBFLGg2MbubLulGXHwTIJgkMWct9949t4nuFNMMpnk9__485yfQIHi9ht2tKX6OeJ1BiwF85wOjO_0N-MbTwf7AbRFv1Dys3xIzYXgQszgClWcO2hW66FDGBu0Yhg7NfZ9r5qX1RqN8cYPWivUizIKEZQzA4Jbh8U3ZG-e-D9SiRaHFUezGNFrMEIj6x64Ukm5LS-slDeKBD68U8XcurQ3wb5KOU6mfjE5MTld19VepX6eTE53JiankBwE_nV8Y_iRAjnk94on8iNAQZ4RVswnj6nykd_2mmzX46IQ6NQD6x7bDhQ-4uWHvVUr_wUAAP__m4mEqA). The commission met yesterday to weigh stiffer penalties.
## FBI Merges Norfolk into Richmond Office
The [_FBI has officially consolidated_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkT2unTAQhVdjOl_hP7guKNLQvbQp0WDGMIqxke0LYvcRSXbwpvw050ifzq-v6QsoUFx_wo5DPf0U8SoBa8U8pQPjnT4ZbywO9gNojX6m5CfZyo4LwYWYwFU6cdLQLIMHjWAbHERvtbLGGNVsQye8N0rJ_m1FZ6wRVtnWzd5KAOuFaWh4-sS_k0q8sF_Qvue3MB28RYdMt7hQTflVNzwprxQJfLjTifnl0t6EYav1KEz9YHJkcryu6yXUoxLT9XwwOUKu5AIyOT6cyTEkB4HJcb8d1fvhKfsUfjM5-pk4RZcRCnKKJ5ZKKzyiPGNJn-yw8A32o6bIc4Kl8P9hnslte4oLdymWFGiBSikyOUoruNDSKQHIlUHJdY-KW91bDq1RrVdCe-2aPCzHRSFQ6Xqm23UHCn8t6zcHOgf5JwAA___9TqZp) its Norfolk Field Office with the Richmond Field Office. The agency said the move unites the resources, expertise, and capabilities of both offices into one team. Officials emphasized that the [_FBI will remain_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykUMuupSAQ_BrcYQTFx4LFbNyd2c7StNBoZxAMcDTn7yfOzf2C27tOPVJVf17LC8hT2H7Dgbpcbgl4Z4-lYFriieET3wk_mA0cJ9AW3ErRLbKRPReCC7GAKXTh0kFltYMOYapQi2Hq2kkp1Va7tuM6NNAoYUw_jeBwVZ0aG9uuRiGOUJF-_MTXyVbUOFicxnUUqodR9Mi6Bi2VmOqy40Vpo0Dg_CdemGoTj8rrvZQzs_YXkzOT833ftVup3uLF5GxiKGAKf2cmZ0foLY_OkcHnT2T2IwbL5PxUfxgr8RCTi_4vNzHk6MlCwcxvKjt_0G9NlbQ9b_Kecj-wrtkOIP8_UPnhlpeW_wIAAP__a8GMrQ) “firmly present” in the Hampton Roads area. Agents, analysts, and specialized staff will continue working daily in the region alongside local partners, while gaining access to a larger integrated team. The consolidation aims to increase investigative capacity against violent crime, cyber threats, counterintelligence, terrorism, and other national security risks. Officials noted recent partnership successes and said the change strengthens rather than reduces the commitment to making Hampton Roads safer.

## First Snow of the Season Is on the Way
The [first snowflakes of the season](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFu7CAQQE-DOywP8L1LQfEbd5s2pcWaYU3CggWTJbl9hK-QqUZ60tO8eb-tNxtiSI83-0RDPq8JW41IhGX1oVSqKbeE7ZGPiNZhscnZVUxi5gAcYLUbhReuMDjjEQXKAQ1ctJJ6voAadqOuIEFPgHiX_p_yUsygldOT0HctlRuC6To4R4Kax81pK9EKAVcl5FUzNaELlMv4kUOiHX38yS8s45afQzQ70VGZ_M_EwsTSWhu3e-0ZnTOx9JWJ5azhPcfbGHlFW3Pi-H3gRuh4yoV2tJU47aHyhvjJtxwdr8kevAMsiX9101CMO1qIMdT5wtT0eNoQz2Poby98GfEbAAD__69uiAc) are expected late this week in the interior Northeast, with upstate New York, Vermont, and New Hampshire most likely to see them as a storm system moves toward the Northeast. The big cities get a soaking instead. Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Washington are in line for a cold, windy rain, heaviest [late Thursday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0QMJjYUFNu4y7ZbWhiPbVYELJjEyt8_kV94U0wzo6N7z7_H_HAhhrT_dU-0tOU54VUjEmGZt1Aq1ZSvhNeez4huxeLS6mYp5MABOMDsPIU3ztCtdkOU2HdoYTSqN8MIqjss6LtZFq01unEbtVj83YASHkYBwwamC7bh4Ds9qOHmV-N6dFKCVrLXhimBa6Bcbv9zSHTgFj_5jeXm87OL9iA6K-v_MDkxOaXPmSu1E5NTAzM5AbQlmJxelbeC7S8XdJWw8IrEKXN_hBh5-ni-lJB2_jorOULeBDA5dcWu5xViDHUYmRL704X4TUC_8_a28icAAP__A7uAuw) into Friday morning, with street flooding possible in New York. Mountain roads from West Virginia to the Adirondacks could turn slick. Then comes the cold, starting today. Temperatures will run 20 to 25 degrees below normal from the Canadian border to the Gulf Coast, with wind chills near freezing in Chicago and Atlanta and a [first hard freeze](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2zAMRb_G3hRYtGPHg4cu2V7XjgYrXcVqFSkQ-SL074vkfcLjSB7w4txfH_sHxxTz7SffsWkoe0aTBFXUPcQqKrm0jHYrjwT2qJw97zTQbKw11u7sND6x295vASCMPTa7rNO4zoud-mO78HAhmt0SaBiGsw9-OQOeaGDyWOY-bq939j2jneaT8yuPYCJ7mWi8rN00wEct9fSnxKwHQvpXnqgnV-592g7Vh3Tjj46uHV1bayd27rOB9fhiOroiv05fKxNKhWNR6ej6djQvyZD4L8SUYPSAEbCUbB5FJP5OMCzGleRRDcdqlOsNKm_SIWvlZMCiqNl85qjwRpQVrwS7ns_rOvV1848WU4oyL9003O4c09tAv9f7c6P_AQAA__-fm5tl), cold enough to kill unprotected plants, in parts of the South. It won't last. Forecasters expect [warmer-than-normal temperatures](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwzAMRL_G3mSYkmNHg4Yu2dK1o0FblKVClgKZiJB-feGgf1BOJA843L2v-3zHEEPaPnEnwy7PieoRiZnK7EI5-Ei5JqpbfkRCSwWTxVn2chQAAmDGlcOTZmitcUSSVEsGJj0oPU4wtN4sdgKghaZ-vfa9dlJfnFzQKXtZltFCG8xpB-9RMIzdajUqQinhOkh11c3Qkw2cS_edQ2JPLr7yk0q35r2NxjM_jkZ9NPLWyFuttXuhz_lUG3k7-5xvQvZUxN-JhcMa6VxTLuwJDxYYqbBwhegnpE2sOVrxZiBguvRKaj10nvfYFmMfNcQYjnFqhn7bMcR3GP4fwqeRvwEAAP__J42HXQ) to return to the East next week.
## House GOP Picks Jim Jordan as New Leader
House Republicans elected Judiciary Chairman [Jim Jordan of Ohio](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OnTAQhZ8GOiNss_wULtLQbdqUyNhjmCvjQfYEJ28f3c0j7GmPdHS-79fn9mkxYjp-2gsMB9oS1BKBGfIWMBcuiWqCetAdwXrINnm7qV6NQkoh5WYd4wObbL0JAAp0C0ZOy6CXcZJDexo9eaf3ad7l0PvwoYKf-2mZlbZKT_vy0aJ5z8mvaDmMnfOL1WCVkvOg9Lw0Qw8emXL3Ikx8Qoh_6YHcObraaE7muzT6R6PWRq211i7QnzfGu2_UelNERlcatb7wEi_K3iaxg6MLikhQxUm_C4iDbvGfUdjAkIWLVMALT5TFQwzCQwDLmA5RGB4QxdmIBdps_F0xRizj1Az9cVmMX-f4e0ofo_4FAAD___15jq0) as their next leader yesterday, 106 to 73 over Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a closed-door secret ballot. Jordan, a Freedom Caucus co-founder, will serve as minority leader when Democrats take control of the House in January. Scalise had been the [No. 2 House Republican](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2yAYhZ8Gb1jmh9phYMhVhdQhXTp0tAj8tokwWECC8vaV00e4Zz3S0fm-v7f5Znzwcf1tdlR1SXPEVgLWinlefC61xNQitjUdAY3DbKIzMwwwUsYoY7Ox1b9wZp1TCyIg71CxSQoux4mJblNSCAH2h5RW2kkuRowwimG8m7sQy4WLzqtzjn3CmRh766ThaADYRQC_SCIGdL6m3D-Sj3XDJbzTC3Nv094FtdV6FMKvBDQB3Vrr9xLPjoDGSJ-FgD6pCOhUN8wE9MPv9JGyM5E2Hwvd0rMgXdNBdx9T9vVN_9PSbCwS0CbT6xU2I79-Ea6T9Y7wn1-nN2zlD-ajy8odzYfgyzgRMay78eFzsH5P60vBvwAAAP__RVqMxg) since 2014. The vote is a rematch of the two men's 2023 battle for speaker, when Scalise won the nomination but withdrew a day later and Jordan's own bid [fell short](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQhZ8Gd0Rm8G9BsdLKXVbbbWlNYLAnImABGytvf5XcR7inPdLR-b5_1_WKHDhuf_BBpvq0RjpLoFopr55zqSWmM9K5pSMQOsoYHa7QwiCVkkqtaCs_aVWNM54ISDdk1Dh3eh5G1TW7sR6RxtsNVOd7NXrt2hFnUP0AfT_ZoWHznlOfaNUNF-tm1IQAaupAT7PoWnJcU77cE8e6kw-v9KR8senRBLPXehShfwlYBCx4s2-Edydg-ZsCV7ZFwHJP2WGUxWLgQtKjJZm8l3v6X0hu6ZDfgBJ9pSxgKTXll9ALO6F_Kz3OU9v3fZONO04Ogcswiq7dHsjh86T-zN_TwFcAAAD__4HZhII) on the floor. Speaker Mike Johnson stepped aside after last week's losses and did not run. _" His ability to communicate is really kind of unrivaled by anybody else in the House right now,"_ said Rep. Scott Fitzgerald of Wisconsin, a Jordan ally. Jordan will lead the Republican response as Democrats prepare investigations of the Trump administration.
## Russia, Ukraine Hold First Talks in Months
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators met in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, yesterday for their [first U.S.-mediated talks](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ_GdI7wzzVQuLjSCmmLbLslOuDj4I2xkX0IytuvklfYaUcazfd9X6crhBjS7Qs2tOTzlPCsEYmwTD6USjXlM-F5y3tEcFggOZhkKw0XggsxwULhgZNonPWIElWDVnSDVoPphG5WOy-tdwY6NM4Zr-bee-Wc_qdF35vZuSbY15x4RwltLosbQCFIKXotVT8w3aILlMvlJ4dEK_r4zA8slyVvTbQr0V6Z-s_kyOQI8_JCeHVMjp-JsCSgkBNEJsdy1BqAH_cCISE_Kt8QicN8cLfCHDhBvFdO5dh2JsdKuTyZGoNj6kOobuhaI0VTrNvPEGOopmO6vW0Q4vsM_U3hw8rfAAAA__99W4cX) since February, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner leading the American delegation. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called it "very productive" but cautioned, _" There's a lot of work to be done in that regard."_ Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the session "constructive and quite substantive." Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on territory, NATO membership, and limits on Ukraine's military. Talks resume today for a second day, with a large-scale prisoner swap reportedly under discussion.

On this day in 1918, the guns of World War I fell silent at the of the eleventh day of the eleventh month. Congress renamed Armistice Day as Veterans Day in 1954 to honor Americans who served in every war. Happy Veterans Day. To everyone who wore the uniform, and to the families who waited at home, thank you. This country is what it is because of you. If you served, or someone you love did, reply and tell us which branch. We'd love to hear your story. Think about everything you do for your car. The oil changes, the premium gas, and the long warm-up on frosty mornings. Some of those habits keep you safe, and some just keep the service bay busy. Today we're counting down the five car habits that truly protect you, and the five that only drain your wallet. One of them costs American drivers more than $2 billion a year. So which side is your routine on? All of that and more on The Flyover Podcast. ! Today's sponsor, , explores the hormonal changes behind thinning hair after 50 and shares a menopause specialist's approach to supporting fuller-looking hair. | First Snow of the Season Is on the Way The are expected late this week in the interior Northeast, with upstate New York, Vermont, and New Hampshire most likely to see them as a storm system moves toward the Northeast. The big cities get a soaking instead. Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Washington are in line for a cold, windy rain, heaviest into Friday morning, with street flooding possible in New York. Mountain roads from West Virginia to the Adirondacks could turn slick. Then comes the cold, starting today. Temperatures will run 20 to 25 degrees below normal from the Canadian border to the Gulf Coast, with wind chills near freezing in Chicago and Atlanta and a , cold enough to kill unprotected plants, in parts of the South. It won't last. Forecasters expect to return to the East next week. House GOP Picks Jim Jordan as New Leader House Republicans elected Judiciary Chairman as their next leader yesterday, 106 to 73 over Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a closed-door secret ballot. Jordan, a Freedom Caucus co-founder, will serve as minority leader when Democrats take control of the House in January. Scalise had been the since 2014. The vote is a rematch of the two men's 2023 battle for speaker, when Scalise won the nomination but withdrew a day later and Jordan's own bid on the floor. Speaker Mike Johnson stepped aside after last week's losses and did not run. " His ability to communicate is really kind of unrivaled by anybody else in the House right now," said Rep. Scott Fitzgerald of Wisconsin, a Jordan ally. Jordan will lead the Republican response as Democrats prepare investigations of the Trump administration. Russia, Ukraine Hold First Talks in Months Russian and Ukrainian negotiators met in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, yesterday for their since February, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner leading the American delegation. The session ran and focused on prisoner exchanges, the return of Ukrainian civilians and children, and security guarantees. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called it "very productive" but cautioned, " There's a lot of work to be done in that regard." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the session "constructive and quite substantive." Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on territory, NATO membership, and limits on Ukraine's military. Talks resume today for a second day, with a large-scale prisoner swap reportedly under discussion. | | Friend, Today on Veterans Day, we take a moment to honor the courageous men and women who stepped forward to wear our nation’s uniform and fight for our freedoms and our nation. As the daughter and granddaughter of Army, Navy, and Air Force veterans, this day is personal — and I treat my role on the Armed Services Committee as an extension of my deepest gratitude to those who serve. 50,000 veterans, active-duty service members, and military families call Maryland’s Third District home. I’ve made it my mission to ensure that promises made to our military personnel are kept. That’s why I’ve spent my first term in Congress fighting to fund mental health services and expand access to high-quality care at military medical facilities like Walter Reed. To every veteran and military family across our communities, our state, and our nation: Thank you for your service, your sacrifice, and your steadfast commitment to our nation. _**-- Cliff**_
* * *
In the United States under Trump, there are few spectacles more gratifying these days than the sight of MAGA lawmakers--including GOP Speaker Mike Johnson-- discovering the country has grown tired of them.
The spectacle has now been made even sweeter with the Democratic victors arriving in Washington, D.C. smiling, energetic, and possessed with the notion that government might actually be conducted in the public interest.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0b12773d-842a-49d6-8481-6f3e1d4c972d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This was the pleasing scene on Capitol Hill as the newly elected Democratic senators and representatives arrived for their orientation meetings. They came carrying their luggage, their hopes, their briefing books, and perhaps a modest supply of aspirin for the headaches that accompany the discovery of how Washington works. The new arrivals looked cheerful, purposeful, positively delighted to be there.
What a wonderful sight.
After years of watching the Republican Party turn Congress into a combination of sleazy traveling circus, Ayn Rand debating society, and badly managed lunatic asylum, the appearance of these new Democrats was like opening the curtains in a room that has been occupied too long by unwashed meth addicts.
You could practically hear the furniture sigh with relief.

Hello Friend, Spiritual strength doesn't come in a single moment. It's built over time. And after more than 40 years of pastoring and preaching God's Word, I've learned that consistent time in Scripture is the key to a grounded, courageous life of faith. That's why I created the brand-new _**[2027 Pathway to Victory Daily Devotional](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2K3TAQhZ9G7mysn2vZhYoEx5BiA2GLLcWsNPYO2JKQZIf79sFk9wUy7TnfwMd5e7EvQDuF7RccaKgUm4t9xjNTuKhCpRhqhCdCjmtJVvRiaDlvObfgKl1oFTTePAQf17FBw_Wk5DRJOTYfBpTQahwUer16r7XS_aCUkxreJ_Xo-4bM_Y_fJ_hDPrpxfB-c8F6tCAOfOFP9mTxU7CgU8lhcjCnFnSq50sW8Nbv5qDUVJr8xsTCxFHRnxi7V646ZWEQvdJvq5X27bZzJpcQzO7QuemRyfvvxnYnhrId1cCSgLTA5e6D9aT1e8faH_bPxj2RyTjmWhK5S2D6jAz2dB5MzHkBffRdDxVCZnH_r9ufra_tl22Tj0x_adyqDZqrfbqhz8Wjqf05wGfE3AAD__yBXmCM),**_ a weekday guide to help you start each day with biblical truth and encouragement. Every devotional in this 260-entry collection was written to help you think biblically, live obediently, and trust God more fully. Whether you're struggling with uncertainty, carrying the weight of past mistakes, or simply seeking God's direction, this resource is designed to meet you right where you are. You'll begin the year by discovering how to embrace the new beginning God offers. You'll turn your attention to Jesus Christ through Holy Week and a study of the end times. You'll follow the early church and see how the Holy Spirit empowered believers to stand firm in their faith. And you'll close the year examining the attitudes that shape your life, learning to find contentment and experiencing the freedom of forgiveness. These are not abstract ideas. They are time-tested truths drawn from over four decades of biblical teaching to help you walk closely with Christ each day. This beautifully produced 532-page devotional features a velvet red leather cover, rich gold and brown foil accents, and larger, easy-to-read print, making it both a meaningful spiritual investment and a joy to use.

name: Molly Gray
subject: Honoring Our Veterans
body:
Dear Peter, Today, on Veterans Day, we honor the brave men and women who have served our country, as well as the families who have stood beside them. Their courage, sacrifice, and commitment to something greater than themselves represent the very best of our nation. We owe our veterans more than our gratitude. We owe them a commitment to ensuring they and their families have access to the care, support, and opportunities they have earned. That commitment is personal to me and my husband, Mike. My dad was a Marine First Lieutenant, and my brother a Marine Corporal who enlisted and served in Iraq. Mike’s father served in the Vietnam War as a Staff Sergeant with the 555th Fighter Squadron (“Triple Nickel”) out of Udorn Air Force Base. Sadly, Nick passed away unexpectedly in June. We are thinking of Nick today, as well as family and friends who have served on active duty, and all those veterans across Vermont and our nation who have sacrificed so much. This morning, I’ll be heading to Montpelier for a Veteran’s Day gathering. Below, I’ve shared some events happening today across Vermont. I encourage you, if you can, to attend an event near your, or find a way that feels meaningful to honor and thank the veterans in your life and community. Very Respectfully, _Molly Gray_
_**Wednesday, November 11 | Veterans Day**_ **Stowe | 8:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m.**

Their courage, sacrifice, and commitment to something greater than themselves represent the very best of our nation. We owe our veterans more than our gratitude. We owe them a commitment to ensuring they and their families have access to the care, support, and opportunities they have earned. That commitment is personal to me and my husband, Mike. body:

Hi Friend,
Today we honor the men and women who put on the uniform and gave their time, their strength, and sometimes everything they had to protect our freedom.
[](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
| | | __ As an Air Force veteran, I know that service reaches far beyond the person in uniform. It reaches the spouses who held down the home front, the children who waited for a parent to return, and the families who carry the cost long after the mission ends.
Over the past year, I met veterans in every corner of this district. Their stories reminded me why this country is worth defending.
If you or someone you love has served, thank you. Our freedom exists because of you.

God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

_Formerly All On The Line_

Peter,
Anti-democracy forces seem to be taking these words to heart: if at first you do not succeed, try, try again.
So now that they’ve failed to block the will of the people from being heard this November, they’re scrambling for new strategies to cheat their way into power.
One of their next big schemes is to target the census.
They are hellbent on making it less accurate — eliminating race and ethnicity, blocking sexual orientation questions as well as trying to not count undocumented immigrants for apportionment, despite the constitutional mandate to count all persons.
Why? Because you can’t draw fair maps without a fair count of the population. Skewing the census is a significant way to tilt the playing field in their favor for future elections. And it interferes with the way funding gets dedicated to different communities based on their populations.
The Trump administration has already proposed changes to the census that would have cataclysmic impacts, from distorting the mapping process to making it harder for communities of color to access healthcare and vital services.

So now that they’ve failed to block the will of the people from being heard this November, they’re scrambling for new strategies to cheat their way into power. One of their next big schemes is to target the census. They are hellbent on making it less accurate — eliminating race and ethnicity, blocking sexual orientation questions as well as trying to not count undocumented immigrants for apportionment, despite the constitutional mandate to count all persons. Why? Because you can’t draw fair maps without a fair count of the population. Skewing the census is a significant way to tilt the playing field in their favor for future elections. And it interferes with the way funding gets dedicated to different communities based on their populations. ## Route 66 Turns 100
Route 66 turns 100 today, although the Museum of Northern Arizona in Flagstaff [notes](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD3uozAUxE9jOiN_YYfCxTZ02XZL9ALPYK3Bkf0SKzn9ir3Cf4qpRjOj35_7fIeY4rn9hgM9wTfMJ7aakAjLfGTasZQM6xETVsonLim_1joroSyXkks5w0LxjbOBbvXaLqMzHXrpRmOE0kZ3u3e4ahvsOkqJD4UqjFIMt8dglHRudLqL_uqTl7QYjOy1uhkDWliHYQgYmBG4Rsqlpx2hxG8-IaRPfmPpl3x0ye9Ez8r0L6YmpqbWWg_fAEdMnyvA1HQtMDVJeZlgair5Rcit5fQqZ-VSCE57rLwh_uWRKn8C7fyBG5y8wZZPTgViYmrqil-fLaYUq3XMiO2AmP7_oJ8ifHv1LwAA__8xQoR8) the road's path predates its official designation as part of the federal highway system. More than 150 years ago, wagon trains following a government expedition led by Edward Beale blazed a trail later followed by railroads and the 1926 highway system. The anniversary comes amid a year-long [centennial celebration](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwVssvmLigaGLt3TtiG7gOr4ShghuYzVPX6Wv0DMf_Yb_1zVcgTKV-yfs6Bleayh49IzM2MJeecPWKqSdMnauBWOu36kHLfV0UuqkVIDI9MRgYUjeTHF2dkCv3Gyt1MaaYfPpIi8WTHJwlojJqHibQcYZlXRR3dJA_u2p94w8WzUafbEWjJwcrucVV2ElJuLaRt4QGr1qgTX_1Ce2MdZ9yH5jfnRhPoRehF6O4xg36lwbxWmC1_sk9BKxMJZCkIVehubT46CcqU9OWHnfgfKfxv8N8fT6NwAA__-WbXPJ) of the Mother Road, highlighting stops and new projects like the Hualapai Tribe and its partners' [plans](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGunjAQBODTQLfINgYehYs0dC9tSmTwGjYxNrKXH4XTR38U5QJvDjD6Zn58zp-WAsXtuz3QsH38HPEuAZkxz0fiHXNO1h0UsHCKuIZ0uTIroXqQEqSc7cr0wlnb2pm2X8dB12jkMGotVKvbejdikKvvxlYPsltGty5ucaJfXOfXRS0fY03m3SffaUWnZdOqD61tK_oBfefRV1qgI0654R1tpidF68Pv9MLcrOmog9mZz1K13yo1VWq677v59fN5mpS3Sk0UHW0Y01XAem8pl0pN_yeISk28I-yXDfa0BJxpQaAChSkEOK_jpLhBxBsCeQSKnIB3KpCCg5wuRuh7OImhcDohRfhnrLNx500hUOmHSovtsBT-ivmrZ7-M-hMAAP__Q-uXKw) to turn the boarded-up Osterman Gas Station in Peach Springs into a Route 66 visitor center. A television news crew's [road trip](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpTAMhZ8GOqP8EaBIsQ3dbLsl8oBziRTIKDEg5ulXzN43WHeW5aPvfH8-pg8MMeyv37iRY_z2005XicRMedoSr5RzwmULkQqnneaYjqVMSigLUoKUE84cTpoM1ovTdh46U5OT3WCMUNroenVDbxbsVa-FHRSJzvt2kMJY37disaKrg3vy5DNatEY2WvXGoBa2I9968pURtAROueGVMIfvtKOPdzopN3Pa6uhW5q9S6V-VGis1XtfV4Ocs2-daqfHpVKkxphkjvJeyYia405Ehp4MJrIXCKd_w8wmc8aRY4J8EeCwArzkdrxXeCMAJZor0mZEJpBBwE-ZSZ7d8XSHGUGxXGfHaMMQfTv5fxadTfwMAAP__CheSpQ) earlier this year found Seligman, Williams, and other towns keeping the road's legacy alive decades after Interstate 40 bypassed them.

| | | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there.
Alone. There was no bathroom.
Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex.
Over. And over. And over. **This is the reality of child trafficking.**

Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...**she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. **They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. **Free.** Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal**.**

body:
Spiritual strength doesn't come in a single moment.

| | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc2OnDAMgJ8m3ED5YWDmwKEV5baVWlXaY5TYnkxUICgxjPr2Fe3OC6yv_j5Ln_z-Zt9cnOMavruFhsx3m4st7DJrqftn5EdIWJ4pY9gjWi11VytVK2UdcDzItq7CAQGdgooG1d_aVpprd6keg7543Rq4kpcdKtDQAXoPHuVFm85dqzic99Q5xijZNpeb9H3X3tW99zePUrTSzZS5ybTtfo7gVnbl9z1loAbSUs3Dg3krwnwRehJ6KgR7pmbjo0k5CD2dFfXGB2IdghJmKmnPQBYSkjDj-7evQnc7LxbcsrkYVmFGdHH-Y5GOxDGtbv4g_pvCjFtOZSPguIaP1UIY90WYkRYXXzyklWllYcYfff3z11S_Yqs84PaM8xxL14tWhlP6l8Of_MAx6L8BAAD__4YglwU)

Hello Friend, Spiritual strength doesn't come in a single moment. It's built over time. And after more than 40 years of pastoring and preaching God's Word, I've learned that consistent time in Scripture is the key to a grounded, courageous life of faith. That's why I created the brand-new _**[2027 Pathway to Victory Daily Devotional](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc2OnDAMgJ8m3ED5YWDmwKEV5baVWlXaY5TYnkxUICgxjPr2Fe3OC6yv_j5Ln_z-Zt9cnOMavruFhsx3m4st7DJrqftn5EdIWJ4pY9gjWi11VytVK2UdcDzItq7CAQGdgooG1d_aVpprd6keg7543Rq4kpcdKtDQAXoPHuVFm85dqzic99Q5xijZNpeb9H3X3tW99zePUrTSzZS5ybTtfo7gVnbl9z1loAbSUs3Dg3krwnwRehJ6KgR7pmbjo0k5CD2dFfXGB2IdghJmKmnPQBYSkjDj-7evQnc7LxbcsrkYVmFGdHH-Y5GOxDGtbv4g_pvCjFtOZSPguIaP1UIY90WYkRYXXzyklWllYcYfff3z11S_Yqs84PaM8xxL14tWhlP6l8Of_MAx6L8BAAD__4YglwU),**_ a weekday guide to help you start each day with biblical truth and encouragement. Every devotional in this 260-entry collection was written to help you think biblically, live obediently, and trust God more fully. Whether you're struggling with uncertainty, carrying the weight of past mistakes, or simply seeking God's direction, this resource is designed to meet you right where you are. You'll begin the year by discovering how to embrace the new beginning God offers. You'll turn your attention to Jesus Christ through Holy Week and a study of the end times. You'll follow the early church and see how the Holy Spirit empowered believers to stand firm in their faith. body:
---
| | Hi team,

Today, on Veterans Day, we pause to honor the brave men and women across New Jersey and our entire country who answered the call to serve.

**Our veterans put everything on the line to defend our freedom, protect our families, and keep our communities safe. Their dedication represents the best of who we are, and we must never take it for granted.**

Honoring our veterans isn’t just about the words we say on November 11th - it’s about following through on the promises we’ve made to them every single day. That means ensuring every veteran has access to quality healthcare, good-paying jobs, stable housing, and the full benefits they’ve earned without bureaucratic delays. We must always have the backs of those who have had ours.

To every veteran and military family in our community: thank you for your selfless service, your sacrifice, and your steadfast commitment to our nation.

— Josh
---
|
---

* * *

**This is about the men who inspired me to become a U.S. Marine. Semper Fi, and Happy Veterans Day.**
* * *
Pleus Hall was one of those typical church meeting halls you find all across Missouri. A large room, usually full of tables, with a kitchen on one end. At Immaculate Conception parish (IC for short) the hall was used for all sorts of gatherings, both on Sunday and throughout the week. It probably still is.
For a stretch of time, before my littlest sister was born, it was used for something quite special to our family. My parents and several of their friends had been deeply involved in running twice-a-month dinners there for anyone who wanted to come. The idea was that people who were struggling to feed themselves and their families would have a reliable place to go a couple times a month. They believed it was a good way to serve the community and made sure us kids were a part of it.
Us kids enjoyed it quite a bit. In nice weather we could even walk, since the hall was only about a third of a mile from our house.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4ce29090-0560-4f46-b52d-edac9f01512e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Me and the family at IC around the time of the dinners
The guy who oversaw the parish kitchen, Al Mueller, made things fun and interesting for all the kids whose parents brought them to help out. First, we would set the tables, and then we would sign up for our nightly duties. Things like helping clean up, gathering trash, re-setting the tables, greeting people, or whatever else needed doing.
When Mr. Al would gather all the kids together to ask us what chores we wanted to do, my sister, who was a year younger than me, and I would shoot up our hands and yell.
"Ooh, ooh, ooh! We want to do the dishes, Mr. Al! We want to do the dishes!"
Mr. Al seemed to think we were a bit nuts, sometimes asking us if we were sure there wasn't something else we'd rather do.
As for me and my sister, we thought _Mr. Al_ was a bit nuts for thinking the dishes was much of a chore. You see, at home, doing the dishes was quite the ordeal. You had to clear them from the table, stack them all up, fill the tubs with water, scrub the dishes clean, rinse them, set them on the counter, and then towel them dry before putting them away. And I can tell you right now, when the person cooking isn't the same one cleaning, there always seems to be a lot more to scrub...
At the parish, on the other hand, they had these things called dishwasher machines, so doing the dishes there was no more than waiting for someone to bring them in from the tables, tossing them into the machine, and pressing a button. We felt like we were totally scamming old Mr. Al!
I'm not sure when it happened, he never let on to us kids, but at some point he figured out why we thought doing the dishes was such a good deal. Eventually, for reasons unknown to me, the dinners ended and we didn't see Al as much anymore.
Then, one day, some time later, there was a knock at the door. All of us kids ran to see who it was and were delighted to see Mr. Al. He talked to my mom for a minute and then he waved us all over to his big blue pickup truck. He climbed up and pointed to something in the bed, smiling. It was a dishwasher!
Al hadn't forgotten our unexpected enthusiasm in doing the dishes back during those dinners and, when he later remodeled the kitchen in his house, he saved his old dishwasher, loaded it up on his truck, and brought it by our house. A friend of his helped him install it for us that afternoon.
Mr. Al didn't have to do that, but he remembered us and sacrificed an entire day bringing his old dishwasher over to our house and installing it. We weren't close family friends, just acquaintances at church, and if it weren't for me writing this, no one else on earth would ever know that he had done it. But he did it anyway.
Many years later, I reconnected with Al when I was trying to figure out how I could best pay back my community for everything they had done for me and my family over the years. Al, a Marine Vietnam veteran, knew exactly what to do. He took me down to the Marine Corps League in Apache Flats, Missouri, way out on the west side of town.
There I met his friends, a crew of Americans who did what their country asked of them, and who never asked for anything in return. I listened to their stories. Of a war their politicians had sent them to, most as draftees, and what it was like coming home after suffering through so much. Several talked about the friends they had lost, including one whose friend had bled out in front of him thousands of miles away. I was shocked at how openly they spoke within the walls of the Marine Corps League.
One old Marine, Ron, a Jeff City High School grad just like me, pulled out his guitar and sang some songs for us. About answering the call for your country. About how their fathers had fought in the second world war and come home heroes. How they thought it would be the same for them, and how very, very different it ended up being for them during and after Vietnam.
He gave me a CD of his songs, called [The Young and the Brave](https://substack.com/redirect/53aee697-f3ce-43a8-93bc-5279716a3259?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I listened to it on loop for weeks and I still have it. These were the guys I looked up to growing up. Our Vietnam vets might not have come home heroes, but they were my heroes. For the selfless service they gave their country and continued to give to their communities, despite what they had gone through.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f66d1c58-1e3f-45fc-9af4-93ecfeca9e2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The Young and The Brave Album Cover_
They inspired me to follow in their footsteps and become a U.S. Marine. And so I did. Al even came all the way out to Quantico, Virginia, for my Officer Candidate School Graduation and gave my mom his old Vietnam Second Lieutenant rank bars to pin onto me at my commissioning ceremony.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c3935965-7a2c-4ded-84b0-4b87436e0849?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Al at my OCS Graduation
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e0203be8-1c5c-4262-9911-fdf965704a4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My Mom pinning on Al's old second lieutenant rank
Before I knew it, I was overseas just like them.
I led a police training team of twelve Marines and a Navy Corpsman in Iraq. I occasionally thought of those old timers when planning our missions outside the wire and I did everything I could to make sure the Marines in my charge, the young and the brave, came home safely. I teared up when I first stepped on American soil after coming home from Iraq, and both times I came home from Afghanistan. I'm sure part of it was the relief of making it home and finally being safe again.
But that's not what I was thinking about. As I walked past volunteers greeting me at the airport and thanking me for my service, all I could think about was my Vietnam vet friends who had deserved this so much more than I did and who never got it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/248a8931-fd69-4a1f-97f6-a26a450e8d01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Leading a mission in Al-Anbar_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcb75255-04be-46b4-8dcc-6f8b1acf98db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_At a local police outpost in rural Afghanistan_
My generation of veterans would have never received that welcome if not for the suffering that our Vietnam vet brothers and sisters went through.
And when people ask me why I joined the Marine Corps, instead of some other service, I think about Al and I tell them, "You never forget the man who saved you 45 minutes of hard labor at the sink every night."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b15bd6b2-a776-4a74-aff9-b1f4f380b2de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Me and Al fixing my grandma 's car on Highway 63 in central Missouri_

Happy Veterans Day,
Lucas

clean_body: Peter, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftiGAP who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're MarxiGAP. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. LeftiGAP focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftiGAP destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! God Bless, Mark Levin Chairman Emeritus Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

subject: The terrain has changed. The calling has not.

In the wake of the election results, today is a good day to remember why we are here.

| | | [](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcuO1TAMhp8m3fUoF_e26AKpFDbDDEKIZeSTmDZSmkSpz_D6qDDwAOPlr0-2P_0_nuwThhjS9gUPmrdciq2n5Z2YasWQdjzdjmkjzzs5tFrqvlWqVcqi4_BKFrDxM2APfd83NKthApCjUUOzz05ObtBwB2c6f7-jNAig5YjQTaC8bsJ8LVTXAHSqu90NYNdN2qCnYZhGAZJ84Fxv12-VzuApccB4c_lo4rwzl1OYD0KvQq_of0baMN5y3YRez0cpubLQq88JmdoD2e0XatYzP6ojlz0JsyglQY2DtHXspND9gw_7FxBmSfiWHOTD4xBmoQNDfAsdHgXDloRZSj65pUiOQ04tlkL4n8qJKbEwy-fn798-2q9D--n55aX9Z9_U2ZdfIcZw9oMAuV0X_ijye0t5nfXvAAAA___7b5t1)

Together](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcuO1TAMhp8m3fUoF_e26AKpFDbDDEKIZeSTmDZSmkSpz_D6qDDwAOPlr0-2P_0_nuwThhjS9gUPmrdciq2n5Z2YasWQdjzdjmkjzzs5tFrqvlWqVcqi4_BKFrDxM2APfd83NKthApCjUUOzz05ObtBwB2c6f7-jNAig5YjQTaC8bsJ8LVTXAHSqu90NYNdN2qCnYZhGAZJ84Fxv12-VzuApccB4c_lo4rwzl1OYD0KvQq_of0baMN5y3YRez0cpubLQq88JmdoD2e0XatYzP6ojlz0JsyglQY2DtHXspND9gw_7FxBmSfiWHOTD4xBmoQNDfAsdHgXDloRZSj65pUiOQ04tlkL4n8qJKbEwy-fn798-2q9D--n55aX9Z9_U2ZdfIcZw9oMAuV0X_ijye0t5nfXvAAAA___7b5t1) Dear Friend, In the wake of the election results, today is a good day to remember why we are here. First, the ultimate battle isn’t about politics or parties. It’s about truth, and the freedom to speak it. ADF exists to remove the obstacles between people and the Gospel. We protect the first freedoms that keep the door open so that all might be free. With God’s grace, we do that regardless of which party is in power. Second, we play the long game. The terrain changes, but the strategy does not. We anticipated this shift, though we hoped it wouldn’t be this big, and that is why—with your partnership—we have pressed so hard in the courts these past few years. We will likely see more hostility toward truth in the days ahead. But we also expect new opportunities to set precedents, especially in states with leaders hostile to human flourishing. Losses at the ballot box in Nevada and Virginia, where voters enshrined a right to abortion in their state constitutions, signal what kinds of policies might soon be attempted elsewhere. We will continue to contend for the sanctity of every woman’s life and that of her unborn child. But truth won on Tuesday, too. It can never be erased, only rediscovered or rejected. And in several states, voters rediscovered the truth that men and women are different. Biology isn’t red or blue. Building on our major victory at the U.S. Supreme Court this year, voters in Arizona and Nebraska approved measures to protect girls’ sports. Arizona’s extended those protections to women’s private spaces. Nebraska’s wrote its women’s sports law into the state constitution. You might expect that from Nebraska or even Arizona. Then came Colorado and Washington. In Colorado, two measures are leading: one protecting girls’ sports, the other protecting children from dangerous transition surgeries. In my home state of Washington, voters appear to have approved a measure protecting girls’ sports. Voters are responding to the stories of girls who paid the price. In Puyallup, Washington, then-15-year-old wrestler Kallie Keeler was sexually assaulted by a male competitor whom state and school policy allowed to compete against her. The state told her it could happen again. Her emergency petition is pending before the U.S. Supreme Court. And in Camas, Washington, a male athlete who switched to the girls’ cross-country team midyear took the final qualifying spot from a deserving young woman from Puyallup High School. He will compete in the women’s state finals this Saturday. I don’t want you to miss this, friend. In 2014, when ADF took on the lie of gender ideology to uphold biological reality, few were with us. Public opinion was at best mixed. This week, the American people crossed political and ideological lines to say otherwise. This tells us the American people aren’t ready to abandon truth. Getting here took hard work, alliance-building, and persuasion. Tragically, it also took many young women paying the cost of a lie. If working at ADF has shown me anything, it is that sometimes you have to lose before you can win. But truth always defeats darkness, and lies have a way of producing harms that become impossible to deny. We are not afraid. We walk into the wind, because that is where God has called us. This is not a time for despair. Hebrews 6:18-19 reminds us it is impossible for God to lie, and it calls the hope we have in Him “a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.” That hope is why the Lord has called ADF to keep the door open for the Gospel. You and I contend for His truth so that all might be free to find that hope and spend eternity with Him. The terrain has changed. The calling has not. Let’s go. | | [DOUBLE MY GIFT](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcuO1TAMhp8m3fUoF_e26AKpFDbDDEKIZeSTmDZSmkSpz_D6qDDwAOPlr0-2P_0_nuwThhjS9gUPmrdciq2n5Z2YasWQdjzdjmkjzzs5tFrqvlWqVcqi4_BKFrDxM2APfd83NKthApCjUUOzz05ObtBwB2c6f7-jNAig5YjQTaC8bsJ8LVTXAHSqu90NYNdN2qCnYZhGAZJ84Fxv12-VzuApccB4c_lo4rwzl1OYD0KvQq_of0baMN5y3YRez0cpubLQq88JmdoD2e0XatYzP6ojlz0JsyglQY2DtHXspND9gw_7FxBmSfiWHOTD4xBmoQNDfAsdHgXDloRZSj65pUiOQ04tlkL4n8qJKbEwy-fn798-2q9D--n55aX9Z9_U2ZdfIcZw9oMAuV0X_ijye0t5nfXvAAAA___7b5t1)

The warning shot came from the most famous tattoo address in America. By 2025, the Sunset Strip -- the boulevard where every actor and rock star got inked between takes -- had become a corridor of dark windows. Pink Taco gone. Le Petit Four gone. Chin Chin gone. A legendary club block sold off for $80 million to a developer known only as "8850 Sunset." Sunset Strip Tattoo, the parlor that outlived hair metal, sits in the middle of that collapse, a bellwether on a boulevard of vacant leases. When the Strip's foot traffic evaporates, the shops that lived off it go with it. The decline announced itself there first -- on the street where tattooing was never just a purchase, it was a sacrament.

By 2025, the Sunset Strip -- the boulevard where every actor and rock star got inked between takes -- had become a corridor of dark windows. Pink Taco gone. Le Petit Four gone. Chin Chin gone. A legendary club block sold off for $80 million to a developer known only as "8850 Sunset." Sunset Strip Tattoo, the parlor that outlived hair metal, sits in the middle of that collapse, a bellwether on a boulevard of vacant leases. When the Strip's foot traffic evaporates, the shops that lived off it go with it. The decline announced itself there first -- on the street where tattooing was never just a purchase, it was a sacrament. | | ---|---|--- Continue reading this post for free in the Substack app | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Heartland Journal 99 E. **Wednesday, November 11, 2026**
More local growers are making themselves known. Along the rural roadsides: small wooden hutches filled with goods, operating on the honor system. Handwritten signs on cardboard, staked near a gate or at a corner: _Eggs for sale._
We raise much of our own food for our kitchen table. For years, we sold what we grew and produced. We understand that production depends on the land, the people available to do the work, and whether what is earned can sustain the effort.
Yesterday, for our dinner table, we stopped at a local farm stand to pick up vegetables not grown in our field.
This reciprocity between people and the land is a model we must carry into how we rebuild our manufacturing and business capacity nationwide. We cannot fortify our productive capacity without protecting its foundations: healthy soil, clean water, and the natural systems that sustain them. The process is inseparable from the product.
How do we expand what we produce without exhausting what sustains us?
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Dear Peter,
**__[Can I have an honest conversation with you?](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=00ebe95bcff0481a9ab60a91386b01af&_e=1EOkjyafT8agMCUMfOa1SVUTMojht48huUE9l0nIzzyJQI99IVV0kVdaCSmd-EMf8ellvfetON2lQahnVfz_41G5VIQuhqVqlMj39boaL_aAU1GRgRSyHr5Hg6aHzsFPZNbnz6LMxx17v1mCLIc6gWIYu-Dg12v5srptZ-ko0ewdRMXlqZ9GtW1jruyABgz9WUr6izaFXllBqfNU9Q5AY4zpXGcGj9yWzu6jAaI820v51Mkrtk5puu6LGVgdrDVx8fSkcpqlO_6JcL-FKQZfn7jlTwEmqi4Mcnax6wy8GeEOLC47tzM2g59lBUVIDylshYa272BVK3JOhhTx0mO--ICM815qGGgGf8CR5wsLInlb35xyc8CBW2PD_uAsLXud33hJrbLtD80dSJJ5JOT9x2g_NRHWaSZXurfgFxgnNG8kvhHg-dMhsJTI_Rgy8kSxJnN0HkmxZj9LOIMuloyX0KXYxwMjzZzczqikQE9OG5yvZzIk02qbG-kXhGWXnqQpQL03OuZkfhgRU21PLXlcWfkU4XO1qSBDghJE3EM3FcE%3D)__**
The midterms weren’t what we expected.
But that doesn’t change the job in front of us.

body:
The numbers tell a remarkable story. Let's keep showing up for our communities.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/c3958889cb84/look-what-we-built-together?e=a4a0e00aa9)

---
| |
Hi Peter,

It’s been a week since Election Day. We may not have gotten the outcome we wanted; there's no pretending otherwise. But before we turn the page, I think we should take a moment to recognize what we accomplished together.
**We moved the needle and there is a lot to celebrate.**
* **The narrowest Republican winning margin since 1992.** Glenn Grothman won with just 52.75% of the vote with a 9.4 percent margin, the smallest margin in the 6th in more than three decades.
* **A 13.2-point shift since 2024.** We substantially narrowed the gap in a district that has been challenging territory for Democrats.
* **43.3% of the vote.** We earned more than four out of every ten votes cast, putting our campaign's result on par with Dan Kohl's 2018 showing.
* **$333,703 raised.** That money came primarily from individual donors, almost entirely from within the 6th District. Thousands of people chose to invest in this campaign, and that is something worth recognizing. It also sets us apart from the campaigns who self-funded or raised large portions of money from out of state billionaires and corporate donors.
* **An increase in our vote share percentage.** Brad won Neenah by a 16.2% margin over Grothman, and Menasha by 17.1%, which helped elect Becky Nichols, and in turn helped flip the Assembly. Other communities shifted the margins too, some by even larger amounts:
* Bayside – 37.5%
* Appleton – 28.1%
* Portage – 24.8%
* Columbus – 24.3%
* Lodi – 23.4%
* Oshkosh – 21.9%
* Sheboygan – 18.6%
* Town of Caledonia – 13.5%
* Beaver Dam – 10.2%
* **A campaign that reached all eleven counties.** We built relationships, showed up in communities, had conversations, and demonstrated that Democratic organizing can gain ground throughout this district. Every one of those counties moved to a more Democratic vote.
* **Volunteers are making waves**. Hundreds of people stepped up to volunteer for our campaign. Many of them are now moving into leadership positions with the Democratic Party and building structure that will last long beyond this campaign.

I ran because I believe the people of this district deserve a representative who puts them ahead of party politics and special interests. That message reached people well beyond our traditional base, and the results demonstrate that there is room for a different kind of politics in the 6th District. I am immensely proud of that and I hope you are too.
To everyone who gave something of themselves to this effort, thank you for trusting me, trusting this team, and believing in what we were trying to accomplish. We may not have won this election, but we built something real.

And our campaign was part of a much bigger story. Across Wisconsin, voters elected David Crowley as governor and every state-wide candidate. Democrats also won control of both chambers of the Wisconsin Legislature, and two congressional seats changed hands. Across the country, voters also delivered major changes in Congress, with Democrats winning control of both the House and Senate. There were historic firsts, new voices entering public service, and communities making their priorities heard. Whatever the outcome in any individual race, there was a tremendous amount of civic energy on display this year, and we should recognize it.

**Let’s keep showing up.**
We hope everyone who found a way to get involved in this campaign will stay involved in their communities. Attend your county board, city council, and school board meetings. Get to know the people serving in your local government, regardless of party. Call or email your elected officials when an issue concerns you. Ask questions, share your experiences, volunteer, and consider serving on a local board or commission yourself. Democracy needs more than participation every few years. It needs people who are willing to show up, pay attention, and make their voices heard throughout the year. Let’s get to work and keep fighting for Wisconsinites.
With gratitude,
Brad and the campaign team
